args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Lender Markup of Counterparty Draft)

Document Status: COUNTERPARTY DRAFT WITH LENDER REQUIRED MODIFICATIONS
Parties: [Secured Party / Administrative Agent] ("Secured Party"); [Debtor / Borrower] ("Company"); [Depository Bank] ("Bank")
Related Facility: Credit Agreement dated as of [●], among Company, the Lenders party thereto, and Secured Party as Administrative Agent (the "Credit Agreement")
Accounts: See Schedule I (Deposit Account Nos. [●] / ABA [●])
Governing Law: State of New York; UCC Article 9 control (N.Y. U.C.C. §§ 9-104, 9-314)
Redline Legend: [DELETE: text to be deleted from counterparty draft]  [INSERT: text to be inserted]  [MOVE]  Comments in {braces}

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TITLE / PREAMBLE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [●], 20[●] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and among:

(i) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF BORROWER / DEBTOR], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Company");

(ii) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT], as administrative agent and collateral agent for the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement referred to below (in such capacities, together with its successors and assigns in such capacities, the "Secured Party"); and

(iii) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF DEPOSITORY BANK], a [national banking association / state bank] (the "Bank").

[INSERT: Reference is made to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of [●], among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto, and the Secured Party, as administrative agent (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), and to the other Loan Documents (as defined in the Credit Agreement). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement, or if not defined therein, in the UCC.]

RECITALS

A. [DELETE: The Company maintains certain deposit accounts with the Bank.] [INSERT: The Company has granted to the Secured Party, for the benefit of the Secured Parties, a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts (as defined below) and all cash, checks, securities entitlements, financial assets, and other property credited thereto from time to time (collectively, the "Account Collateral"), pursuant to the Guarantee and Collateral Agreement dated as of [●] (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Security Agreement").]

B. [INSERT: The Credit Agreement and the Security Agreement require the Company to cause the Deposit Accounts to be subject to a control agreement in favor of the Secured Party in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party, in order to perfect the Secured Party's security interest by "control" within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and 9-314 of the UCC.]

C. The parties desire to enter into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Account Collateral by control and to set forth their respective rights and obligations with respect to the Deposit Accounts.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 1.1 Definitions. As used in this Agreement:

"Account Collateral" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals. [INSERT: For the avoidance of doubt, Account Collateral includes all "deposit accounts" (as defined in the UCC) identified on Schedule I, all funds on deposit therein, all security entitlements and financial assets credited thereto, all interest, dividends, and distributions thereon, and all proceeds of the foregoing.]

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or the city in which the Bank's office maintaining the Deposit Accounts is located] are authorized or required by law to close.

[INSERT: "Control Notice" (also referred to as a "Notice of Exclusive Control" or "NOEC") means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A, stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Deposit Accounts.]

[INSERT: "Excluded Account" means any deposit account that is an Excluded Account under (and as defined in) the Credit Agreement or Security Agreement, including (without limitation) (i) payroll, benefits, and trust accounts holding solely funds for payment of wages, employee benefits, or taxes, (ii) zero-balance accounts swept daily to a Controlled Account, (iii) petty cash accounts with average daily balances not exceeding the de minimis threshold set forth in the Credit Agreement, and (iv) accounts maintained solely for cash collateral for letters of credit or hedging obligations permitted under the Credit Agreement; provided that no account listed on Schedule I is an Excluded Account.]

"Deposit Accounts" means each deposit account maintained by the Company with the Bank and identified on Schedule I hereto, [INSERT: as such Schedule I may be amended or supplemented from time to time by written agreement of the parties (or by notice from the Company and Secured Party to the Bank adding accounts),] together with any successor, renumbered, or replacement account, and any account into which funds from any such account are transferred by the Bank other than pursuant to instructions of the Company that are permitted hereunder prior to delivery of a Control Notice.

[DELETE: "Instructions" means any instructions from the Company regarding the Deposit Accounts.]
[INSERT: "Instructions" means entitlement orders, instructions, directions, or other orders with respect to the disposition of funds or other property in the Deposit Accounts, whether originated by the Company or the Secured Party.]

"Secured Obligations" [DELETE: means the obligations of the Company to the Secured Party.] [INSERT: means all Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement), including without limitation all unpaid principal of and accrued and unpaid interest on the Loans, all LC Exposure, all accrued and unpaid fees, and all expenses, reimbursements, indemnities, and other obligations of the Loan Parties to any Secured Party arising under the Loan Documents or secured by the Collateral, whether direct or indirect, absolute or contingent, due or to become due, now existing or hereafter arising.]

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York [INSERT: ; provided that if by reason of mandatory provisions of law, perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority of any security interest is governed by the UCC as in effect in a jurisdiction other than New York, "UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in such other jurisdiction for purposes of the provisions hereof relating to such perfection, effect, or priority].

[INSERT: Section 1.2 UCC Terms. Terms defined in Article 8 or 9 of the UCC and not otherwise defined herein have the meanings assigned in the UCC, including "control," "deposit account," "entitlement order," "financial asset," "proceeds," and "security entitlement."]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE II — THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS; CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 2.1 Identification of Accounts; Account Details.
(a) The Bank confirms that the Company is the Bank's customer with respect to each Deposit Account listed on Schedule I, and that Schedule I correctly sets forth the account name, account number, and office/location for each Deposit Account.
(b) [INSERT: The Company and the Bank shall not change the account name or account number of any Deposit Account, or transfer any Deposit Account to another office of the Bank, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, except for changes required by the Bank's internal systems that are promptly notified in writing to the Secured Party and that do not impair control.]
(c) [INSERT: The Bank represents and warrants that (i) each Deposit Account is a "deposit account" as defined in Section 9-102 of the UCC, (ii) the Bank is a "bank" as defined in Section 9-102 of the UCC, and (iii) the State of New York is the Bank's jurisdiction for purposes of Section 9-304 of the UCC with respect to each Deposit Account (or, if different, the jurisdiction is as set forth on Schedule I and is acceptable to the Secured Party).]

Section 2.2 Establishment of Control.
(a) The Bank agrees that it will comply with [DELETE: instructions originated by the Company or, following notice, the Secured Party] [INSERT: Instructions originated by the Secured Party concerning the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Company]. The Bank hereby agrees that it will not comply with any Instructions originated by the Company [INSERT: or any other person other than the Secured Party] concerning the Deposit Accounts after the Bank's receipt of a Control Notice, except as otherwise expressly provided in Section 2.4 (Permitted Ordinary-Course Activity Prior to Control Notice) and Section 3.2 (Priority of Bank's Claims).
(b) [INSERT: The parties acknowledge and agree that this Agreement is intended to confer, and does confer, "control" of each Deposit Account upon the Secured Party within the meaning of Sections 9-104(a)(2) and 9-314 of the UCC, and that the Secured Party's security interest in the Account Collateral is perfected by control.]
(c) [DELETE: The Company may continue to operate the accounts in the ordinary course until the Bank receives contrary instructions.]
[INSERT: Until the Bank receives a Control Notice from the Secured Party, the Company may operate the Deposit Accounts and the Bank may honor Instructions originated by the Company, subject to Section 2.4 and the Bank's standard account documentation solely to the extent not inconsistent with this Agreement. This Agreement controls in the event of any conflict with the Bank's standard terms and conditions or account agreements (the "Account Agreements"), and the Bank's Account Agreements are hereby amended to the extent necessary to give effect to this Agreement.]

Section 2.3 Notice of Exclusive Control.
(a) The Secured Party may deliver a Control Notice to the Bank at any time. [INSERT: The Secured Party shall simultaneously send a copy of any Control Notice to the Company; provided that failure to send such copy shall not affect the validity or effectiveness of the Control Notice as against the Bank or the Company.]
(b) [INSERT: The Bank shall confirm receipt of a Control Notice in writing (including by email) to the Secured Party within one (1) Business Day of receipt, and shall implement exclusive control no later than the opening of business on the Business Day following the Business Day of receipt (or immediately, if the Control Notice so states and is received during the Bank's business hours).]
(c) [DELETE: The Bank may require a reasonable period to implement exclusive control.] [INSERT: Time periods for implementation of exclusive control shall not exceed those stated in clause (b); "reasonable period" concepts in the Bank's form are deleted as inconsistent with market and Credit Agreement requirements.]
(d) [INSERT: After receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall neither accept nor comply with any Instruction originated by the Company (including automated sweeps, ACH, wire, check, or online banking Instructions), and shall comply solely with Instructions originated by the Secured Party, without further consent by the Company.]

Section 2.4 Permitted Activity Prior to Control Notice; Sweeps and Dispositions.
(a) [INSERT: Prior to receipt of a Control Notice, the Company may make withdrawals, transfers, and other dispositions of funds in the Deposit Accounts in the ordinary course of business, and the Bank may permit automated sweeping arrangements disclosed on Schedule I (if any), in each case solely to the extent not prohibited by the Credit Agreement or Security Agreement.]
(b) [INSERT: Without limiting the Secured Party's rights, the Company shall not close any Deposit Account, or open any additional deposit account with the Bank that is required to be a Controlled Account under the Credit Agreement, without prior written notice to the Secured Party and, for additional Controlled Accounts, execution of a joinder or supplement to this Agreement (or a separate control agreement) in form satisfactory to the Secured Party.]
(c) [DELETE: The Bank may freeze the accounts upon any internal compliance hold or legal process without notice to the Secured Party.]
[INSERT: The Bank shall give the Secured Party prompt written notice (and in any event within one (1) Business Day) of (i) any legal process, freeze, hold, levy, garnishment, or similar action affecting any Deposit Account or Account Collateral, (ii) any claim of adverse ownership or control asserted against any Deposit Account, (iii) any default or termination under the Account Agreements, and (iv) any resignation or termination of the Bank's role as depository. The Bank shall not exercise any freeze or hold rights arising solely under the Account Agreements in a manner that impairs the Secured Party's control rights under this Agreement, except as required by mandatory law or valid legal process, in which case the notice obligation above applies.]

Section 2.5 Statements; Access; Information.
[INSERT: The Bank shall send to the Secured Party, at the address (including email) set forth in Section 6.1, duplicate copies of all account statements, debit/credit advices, and other account communications that the Bank sends to the Company with respect to the Deposit Accounts, and shall provide the Secured Party online view access to the Deposit Accounts upon reasonable request. The Company hereby authorizes such delivery and access. The Bank's failure to provide statements shall not impair the Secured Party's security interest or control.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE III — BANK'S RIGHTS, SUBORDINATION, AND LIMITED LIABILITY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 3.1 Bank's Rights Limited; No Other Agreements.
[INSERT: Except for the Bank's rights expressly preserved in Section 3.2, the Bank subordinates any security interest, right of setoff, recoupment, banker’s lien, or other claim it may have in or against the Deposit Accounts or Account Collateral to the security interest and control rights of the Secured Party. The Bank represents that it has not entered into, and agrees that it will not enter into, any other agreement with any person by which the Bank is obligated to comply with Instructions originated by any person other than the Company (prior to a Control Notice) or the Secured Party (at any time) concerning the Deposit Accounts.]

Section 3.2 Priority of Certain Bank Claims (Carve-Out).
The Bank may exercise setoff, recoupment, or charge rights against the Deposit Accounts solely for:
(i) [DELETE: any and all obligations of the Company to the Bank, of any nature whatsoever;]
[INSERT: the face amount of items deposited to a Deposit Account and returned unpaid, whether for insufficient funds or any other reason;]
(ii) [INSERT: settlement adjustments and corrections for crediting errors with respect to the Deposit Accounts;]
(iii) [INSERT: the Bank's customary account maintenance, transaction, and wire fees with respect to the Deposit Accounts (but not credit facility, loan, or other unrelated fees or indebtedness); and]
(iv) [INSERT: amounts advanced by the Bank as an overdraft accommodation on a Deposit Account, not to exceed at any time the amount of such overdraft, and solely to the extent created in the ordinary course;]
provided that (A) the aggregate amount subject to clauses (iii) and (iv) shall not exceed $[●] / customary amounts without prior notice to the Secured Party, (B) [INSERT: after receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall not permit additional overdrafts and shall not exercise setoff for amounts other than returned items and corrections relating to pre-notice activity without the Secured Party's prior written consent, except as required by mandatory law,] and (C) [INSERT: the Bank's rights under this Section 3.2 are subordinate in priority to the Secured Party's security interest except to the extent of the specific carve-outs listed above, which carve-outs shall have priority only as expressly stated].

[DELETE: Broad "banker's lien and setoff for all obligations" language in Bank form §§ __.]

Section 3.3 Bank's Standard of Care; Limitation of Liability.
(a) The Bank undertakes to perform only such duties as are expressly set forth herein [INSERT: and those mandated by applicable law that cannot be waived, including duties arising from its agreement to comply with the Secured Party's Instructions].
(b) [DELETE: The Bank shall have no liability except for its gross negligence or willful misconduct as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.]
[INSERT: The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in accordance with this Agreement or Instructions believed by the Bank in good faith to be genuine and authorized, except to the extent resulting from the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement, as determined by a final non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction (or as otherwise agreed). Nothing herein shall exculpate the Bank for failure to comply with a Control Notice or Secured Party Instructions after effective receipt, or for honoring Company Instructions in violation of Section 2.3.]
(c) [INSERT: In no event shall any party be liable for special, indirect, consequential, or punitive damages, whether or not advised of the possibility thereof; provided that this limitation shall not apply to (i) the Company's indemnification obligations, (ii) the Bank's failure to comply with a Control Notice or Secured Party Instructions after receipt, or (iii) any party's fraud or willful misconduct.]
(d) [DELETE: The Company alone indemnifies the Bank for all claims arising out of this Agreement.]
[INSERT: The Company agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Bank and its officers, directors, and employees from and against any and all claims, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable out-of-pocket attorneys' fees) arising out of this Agreement or the Bank's actions hereunder, except to the extent resulting from the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement. The Secured Party shall not have any indemnification obligation to the Bank except for losses resulting solely from the Secured Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct in originating Instructions.]

Section 3.4 Interpleader; Conflicting Claims.
[INSERT: If the Bank receives conflicting Instructions or adverse claims with respect to any Deposit Account, the Bank may interplead the funds with a court of competent jurisdiction and thereafter be fully discharged from liability with respect to such funds, after giving prompt notice to the Company and the Secured Party. Pending resolution, the Bank shall maintain the funds in the applicable Deposit Account and shall not release them except pursuant to court order or joint written Instruction of the Secured Party and the Company (or the Secured Party alone after a Control Notice).]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE IV — COMPANY OBLIGATIONS; NEGATIVE COVENANTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 4.1 Security Interest Acknowledgment.
The Company acknowledges and agrees that (i) the Secured Party has a security interest in the Account Collateral securing the Secured Obligations, (ii) this Agreement perfects such security interest by control, and (iii) [INSERT: the Company has no authority to terminate, amend, or waive any provision of this Agreement in a manner adverse to the Secured Party without the Secured Party's prior written consent].

Section 4.2 No Other Control Agreements; No Adverse Claims.
[INSERT: The Company represents that it has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any control agreement or similar arrangement with respect to any Deposit Account in favor of any person other than the Secured Party (except for control arrangements expressly permitted under the Credit Agreement for junior or permitted lienholders with an intercreditor agreement in form satisfactory to the Secured Party). The Company shall not grant or permit any lien on the Account Collateral except Permitted Liens (as defined in the Credit Agreement) that are junior to the Secured Party's security interest or otherwise permitted with the priority contemplated by the Loan Documents.]

Section 4.3 Further Assurances.
[INSERT: The Company and the Bank shall execute and deliver such additional documents and take such further actions as the Secured Party may reasonably request to perfect, maintain, protect, or enforce the Secured Party's security interest and control in the Account Collateral, or to carry out the purposes of this Agreement.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE V — TERM; TERMINATION; RESIGNATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 5.1 Termination.
(a) [DELETE: This Agreement may be terminated by the Company or the Bank upon 30 days' prior written notice to the other parties.]
[INSERT: This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until the earliest of:
(i) written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank that (A) all Secured Obligations have been paid in full in cash (other than contingent indemnification obligations not yet due), all commitments under the Credit Agreement have terminated, and all Letters of Credit have expired or been cash-collateralized in accordance with the Credit Agreement, or (B) the Secured Party otherwise releases its security interest in the Account Collateral;
(ii) written agreement of the Secured Party, the Company, and the Bank; or
(iii) transfer of all funds and closure of all Deposit Accounts with the prior written consent of the Secured Party and distribution of remaining funds in accordance with the Secured Party's Instructions.]
(b) [INSERT: The Company may not terminate this Agreement or close the Deposit Accounts without the Secured Party's prior written consent while any Secured Obligations or commitments remain outstanding.]
(c) [INSERT: Termination of this Agreement shall not affect rights and obligations accrued prior to termination, including the Bank's obligations with respect to funds held as of termination and the indemnities in Section 3.3.]

Section 5.2 Resignation or Replacement of Bank.
[INSERT: The Bank may resign as depository with respect to the Deposit Accounts upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Company and the Secured Party; provided that no such resignation shall become effective until a successor depository bank reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party has executed a control agreement in form and substance substantially identical to this Agreement (or otherwise satisfactory to the Secured Party) and the Deposit Accounts (or successor accounts) are under the Secured Party's control. The Company shall promptly establish replacement Controlled Accounts and cause execution of a replacement control agreement upon any Bank resignation or upon the Secured Party's reasonable request following a material breach by the Bank of this Agreement.]

Section 5.3 Successor Secured Party.
[INSERT: The Bank agrees that the rights of the Secured Party hereunder may be assigned or transferred to any successor administrative agent or collateral agent under the Credit Agreement upon written notice to the Bank (without requirement of Company consent), and the Bank shall recognize such successor as the "Secured Party" hereunder. The Secured Party may also assign its rights hereunder in connection with an assignment of the Secured Obligations permitted under the Credit Agreement.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE VI — MISCELLANEOUS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 6.1 Notices.
All notices, Control Notices, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, certified mail, or email (with confirmation of receipt, except that Control Notices shall be effective upon actual receipt by the Bank whether or not confirmed), addressed as follows:

If to the Company: [●]  Attn: [●]  Email: [●]
If to the Secured Party: [●]  Attn: Agency / Collateral Services  Email: [●]  with a copy to counsel: [●]
If to the Bank: [●]  Attn: [Deposit Account Control / Collateral Services]  Email: [●]  (and such other addresses as appear on the Bank's acceptance or Schedule I)

[INSERT: Notices to the Bank of Control Notices must be delivered to the specific notice addresses designated by the Bank for control notices on Schedule I or in the Bank's signature block; ordinary account officer addresses alone are insufficient unless expressly designated for Control Notices.]

Section 6.2 Amendments; Waivers.
[INSERT: No amendment, modification, termination (except as provided in Section 5.1), or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the Secured Party, the Company, and the Bank (except that the Secured Party and the Bank may amend provisions that solely affect their respective rights and duties as between themselves without the Company's consent, with notice to the Company).]

Section 6.3 Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial.
(a) This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York [INSERT: , without regard to conflicts-of-law principles that would require application of the laws of another jurisdiction (other than mandatory UCC choice-of-law rules for perfection and priority)].
(b) [INSERT: Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, for any action arising out of this Agreement, and waives any objection based on venue or forum non conveniens.]
(c) [INSERT: EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW ANY RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE ACCOUNT COLLATERAL.]

Section 6.4 Entire Agreement; Conflict with Account Agreements.
[INSERT: This Agreement, together with Schedule I and Exhibit A, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to control of the Deposit Accounts and supersedes all prior agreements on such subject. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and any Account Agreement or the Bank's standard form terms, this Agreement shall control. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement or Security Agreement as between the Company and the Secured Party, the Credit Agreement or Security Agreement shall control as between those parties, but shall not expand the Bank's duties without the Bank's consent.]

Section 6.5 Severability; Counterparts; Electronic Signatures.
[INSERT: If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall continue in full force. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (including PDF/electronic counterparts), each of which shall be deemed an original. Electronic signatures (including DocuSign or similar) shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes.]

Section 6.6 No Third-Party Beneficiaries; Secured Parties.
[INSERT: The Secured Parties (as defined in the Credit Agreement) are express third-party beneficiaries of the Secured Party's rights under this Agreement. Except as expressly provided, there are no third-party beneficiaries.]

Section 6.7 Irrevocable Agreements as to Control.
[INSERT: The agreements of the Bank in Sections 2.2 and 2.3 are irrevocable and coupled with the Secured Party's security interest, and the Company has no right to terminate, revoke, or modify the Bank's obligation to comply with the Secured Party's Instructions while this Agreement remains in effect.]

Section 6.8 Expenses.
[INSERT: The Company shall pay all reasonable and documented out-of-pocket fees and expenses of the Bank and the Secured Party (including reasonable attorneys' fees) in connection with the negotiation, execution, administration, enforcement, and amendment of this Agreement, consistent with the expense provisions of the Credit Agreement.]

Section 6.9 USA PATRIOT Act; Sanctions; KYC.
[INSERT: The Bank hereby notifies the parties that pursuant to the requirements of the USA PATRIOT Act, it may be required to obtain, verify, and record information identifying the Company and the Secured Party. Each party agrees to provide such information as reasonably requested for KYC/AML compliance. Nothing in this Agreement requires the Bank to violate sanctions or applicable law.]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCHEDULE I — DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Bank Name: [Depository Bank Full Legal Name]
Bank Jurisdiction (UCC § 9-304): State of New York [confirm]
Bank Notice Address for Control Notices: [specific address / email / fax designated for NOECs]
Bank Ordinary Operations Contact: [●]

| Account Name              | Account Number | Account Type / Purpose        | Location / ABA     | Sweep Arrangement (if any) |
|---------------------------|----------------|-------------------------------|--------------------|----------------------------|
| [Company] Operating Acct  | [●]            | Concentration / Operating     | [●] / [●]          | [None / describe]          |

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty / Depository Bank Draft Review

TO:        File; Deal Team; [Administrative Agent / Client]
FROM:      Banking & Finance — Contracts Desk
DATE:      [●]
RE:        Review of Counterparty/Bank Form Account Control Agreement against Internal ACA Playbook, Executed Credit Agreement, Bank Standard Form, Account Details, and Related Correspondence/Checklists
MATTER:    Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
RELATED:   aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline incorporating all required modifications)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement (the "Draft ACA"), which is substantially based on the depository bank's standard form, against:

  (1) the Firm's internal Account Control Agreement Playbook (the "Playbook");
  (2) the executed Credit Agreement and Guarantee and Collateral Agreement (the "Security Agreement"), including Controlled Account, perfection, and further-assurances covenants;
  (3) the depository bank's standard form ACA and Account Agreements;
  (4) the account schedule / account opening details for the proposed Controlled Accounts; and
  (5) related correspondence and closing checklists identifying ACA execution as a condition precedent or post-closing deliverable.

Bottom line: The Draft ACA does not establish reliable UCC Article 9 "control" on market Agent-protective terms. It contains multiple High and Medium risk deviations — including defective or ambiguous control language, broad bank setoff seniority, unilateral termination rights, delayed or discretionary implementation of exclusive control, Company-only indemnity, missing NOEC mechanics/exhibit, missing subordination of competing control arrangements, and weak conflict language versus the Bank's Account Agreements. As drafted, the Secured Party faces material perfection, priority, and practical enforcement risk, and the Loan Documents' Controlled Account covenant is not satisfied in form and substance.

The companion deliverable aca-redline.docx incorporates all required deletions, insertions, and mechanical fixes. We recommend circulating the redline as the opening Agent mark and holding the positions in Section V (Recommended Positions) and the Summary Deviation Matrix (Section VII).

Risk tally (unique issues):  High: 8  |  Medium: 9  |  Low: 5  |  Total: 22

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. REVIEW STANDARD AND MATERIALS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Playbook Requirements (core)
  • Express agreement by Bank to comply with Secured Party entitlement orders/Instructions without further Customer consent (UCC § 9-104(a)(2)).
  • Irrevocable control undertakings coupled with the security interest.
  • NOEC / Control Notice form attached; clear post-notice freeze on Customer Instructions; short, fixed implementation timeline.
  • Subordination of banker's lien/setoff except narrow returned-item, correction, customary account fees, and limited ordinary-course overdraft carve-outs.
  • No unilateral Customer or Bank termination while Secured Obligations/commitments remain; termination only on Agent release, payoff, or tri-party agreement.
  • ACA controls over Bank Account Agreements on conflict.
  • NY law; Manhattan forum; jury waiver; successor Agent recognition; further assurances; statements and view-access to Agent; notice of adverse claims/legal process.
  • Alignment of "Secured Obligations" to Credit Agreement "Obligations"; Excluded Accounts carved out consistently with Loan Documents.
  • Bank resignation conditioned on successor control agreement acceptable to Agent.

B. Credit Agreement / Security Agreement Touchpoints
  • Controlled Accounts must be subject to control agreements in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.
  • Perfection by control required for deposit-account collateral; springing or continuous control as specified in the facility.
  • Negative pledge / permitted liens architecture requires Agent priority on deposit accounts that are not Excluded Accounts.
  • Further assurances and post-closing controlled-account clean-up covenants.
  • Cash management / blocked account mechanics (if any) must not be undermined by ACA setoff or termination terms.

C. Bank Form / Account Details / Correspondence
  • Bank form favors broad setoff, discretionary timing, Customer-centric indemnity, and easy exit — classic depository paper.
  • Account details must correctly identify each non-Excluded deposit account at the Bank required to be controlled; Control Notice address must be operationally correct.
  • Checklist items: ACA fully executed prior to funding or within post-closing window; Schedule I complete; Exhibit A attached.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ISSUE 1 — Control Language / UCC § 9-104(a)(2) Mechanics
Sections: Draft ACA §§ 2 / operative control covenants (Bank form "instructions" clause)
Playbook: Mandatory express Bank agreement to comply with Secured Party Instructions without further Customer consent; acknowledgment that agreement confers "control."
Deviation: Draft states Bank will follow Customer instructions and, only after some notice, "may" or will follow Secured Party instructions, often still framed as dual-authority or requiring Customer cooperation. Missing clean "without further consent by the Company" formulation and missing express control acknowledgment.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Failure to obtain statutory control → security interest in deposit accounts may be unperfected or junior to a subsequent controlling secured party or a lien creditor/bankruptcy trustee challenge. Direct impairment of CP Controlled Account condition and Agent's priority story.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Playbook control formulation and express UCC §§ 9-104(a)(2), 9-314 acknowledgment (see Redline § 2.2). Non-negotiable for sign-off on "form and substance satisfactory."

ISSUE 2 — Notice of Exclusive Control — Timing and Effectiveness
Sections: Draft ACA notice/exclusive control provisions
Playbook: Control Notice effective on receipt; Bank confirms within 1 Business Day; exclusive control implemented by next open of business (or immediately if specified); no open-ended "reasonable time."
Deviation: Bank form uses "reasonable period to implement," unclear receipt rules, and may condition effectiveness on internal authentication procedures without outside-facing timing.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: During any implementation gap, Customer can drain accounts; Agent's practical remedy set is hollow at the moment of default. Also creates disputes over when Bank liability attaches.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE fixed outside timing as in Redline § 2.3; authentication procedures may be retained only if they do not extend the outside date and emergency email/hand-delivery paths are specified on Schedule I.

ISSUE 3 — Post-NOEC Customer Instructions / Automated Channels
Sections: Draft ACA operating covenants; interaction with online banking, ACH, sweeps, checks
Playbook: After NOEC, Bank complies solely with Secured Party Instructions; all Customer-originated channels (including automated sweeps/ACH/online) freeze unless Agent expressly permits.
Deviation: Draft often freezes only "manual" wires or is silent on ACH debits, check stock, and pre-existing sweep instructions.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Residual leakage post-NOEC defeats blocked-account enforcement and may violate cash dominion features of the Credit Agreement.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE express multi-channel freeze (Redline § 2.3(d)); disclose existing sweeps on Schedule I; Agent consent for any post-NOEC permitted debit types.

ISSUE 4 — Conflict with Bank Account Agreements
Sections: Draft ACA miscellaneous / "subject to account terms" clauses
Playbook: ACA expressly controls over Account Agreements and standard terms.
Deviation: Draft incorporates Bank's standard terms and often provides that Account Agreements govern on conflict or remain "unmodified."
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Hidden setoff, freeze, indemnity, governing-law, and termination terms in Account Agreements can silently override hard-fought ACA protections.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE supremacy clause (Redline §§ 2.2(c), 6.4). Bank may keep Account Agreements for ordinary operations solely to the extent not inconsistent.

ISSUE 5 — Bank Setoff / Banker's Lien Breadth
Sections: Draft ACA Bank rights / priority section
Playbook: Subordination of all Bank claims except: returned items; crediting corrections; customary account-level fees; limited ordinary-course overdrafts. No setoff for loans, derivatives, multi-product exposure, or "all obligations."
Deviation: Bank form preserves setoff and banker's lien for any and all obligations of Customer to Bank, often with priority over Agent.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: At enforcement, Bank can empty Controlled Accounts to cover unrelated credit exposure, priming Agent and eroding collateral value. Direct conflict with first-priority security interest required by Loan Documents.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE narrow carve-out stack in Redline § 3.2. Accept modest dollar cap discussion on fees/overdrafts; reject "all obligations" and affiliate-exposure setoff. Post-NOEC, no new overdrafts and no expanded setoff without Agent consent.

ISSUE 6 — Unilateral Termination / Account Closure
Sections: Draft ACA term and termination
Playbook: No Customer or Bank unilateral termination while facility is outstanding; termination only on Agent written release/payoff, tri-party agreement, or consented account migration with continuing control.
Deviation: Draft permits Customer and/or Bank to terminate on 30 days' notice (or similar).
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Control can disappear on the eve of default or during workout; re-perfection race; potential CP breach without practical cure if Bank walks.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 5.1 structure. Bank resignation (separate from termination of control) only with successor control agreement acceptable to Agent (Issue 7).

ISSUE 7 — Bank Resignation Without Successor Control
Sections: Draft ACA (often silent) / Bank form exit rights
Playbook: Resignation effective only when successor depository has executed a satisfactory control agreement and accounts remain under Agent control.
Deviation: Silent or resignation on notice without successor condition.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Orphaned accounts; temporary loss of control perfection; emergency account-opening under default stress.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 5.2. Company covenant to stand up replacement Controlled Accounts promptly.

ISSUE 8 — Secured Obligations Definition Misaligned
Sections: Draft ACA definitions
Playbook: "Secured Obligations" (or equivalent) must track Credit Agreement "Obligations" — principal, interest, LC exposure, fees, hedge/bank product obligations secured by the Security Agreement, expenses, indemnities — present and future.
Deviation: Draft uses narrow formulation (e.g., "obligations of Company to Secured Party under this Agreement" or a single named loan).
Risk Rating: HIGH
Exposure: Argument that control/security supports only a subset of facility obligations; marshalling and release disputes; mismatch with Security Agreement secured obligations clause.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE cross-reference definition in Redline § 1.1; do not restate a closed list that can drift from the Credit Agreement.

ISSUE 9 — Indemnity and Liability Allocation
Sections: Draft ACA indemnity / standard of care
Playbook: Company indemnifies Bank except for Bank gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach; Agent is not a general indemnitor of Bank; Bank remains liable for failure to honor Control Notice/Agent Instructions; consequential-damages waiver with carve-outs for failure to control, fraud, willful misconduct.
Deviation: Company-only broad indemnity; Bank liability limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct "as finally determined by a court," often without material-breach or failure-to-honor-NOEC carve-outs; sometimes seeks Agent indemnity.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Bank moral hazard on NOEC compliance; Agent foot-fault indemnity risk; expensive "final judgment" precondition before Bank has skin in the game.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 3.3. May accept "final non-appealable judgment" language if failure-to-honor-NOEC and material breach remain inside the liability net. Reject Agent indemnity except for Agent's own gross negligence/willful misconduct in originating Instructions.

ISSUE 10 — Missing Exhibit A (Form of Control Notice)
Sections: Draft ACA exhibits (missing)
Playbook: Agreed form of NOEC attached as exhibit to avoid authenticity and content disputes.
Deviation: No form exhibit; "notice in writing" only.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Bank challenges adequacy of notice in a default scenario; delay while form is negotiated under fire.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Exhibit A as in Redline; Bank may add authentication footer if it does not alter operative instructions.

ISSUE 11 — Schedule I Completeness / Excluded Accounts
Sections: Account schedule; Credit Agreement Excluded Account definition
Playbook: All non-Excluded Bank accounts required to be controlled are listed; payroll/tax/trust/ZBA/petty cash Excluded Accounts stay off schedule; representation that schedule is complete as to Controlled Accounts at Bank.
Deviation: Incomplete numbers, missing ABA/location, inclusion of payroll accounts, or omission of collections DDAs; no completeness rep.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Uncontrolled accounts → covenant default and perfection gaps; accidental control over trust/payroll funds → Bank and Company operational/ERISA-type issues.
Recommended Position: Complete Schedule I from account details; add completeness rep and Excluded Account definition alignment (Redline § 1.1, Schedule I note). Confirm ZBA architecture so only concentration accounts need control if Credit Agreement permits.

ISSUE 12 — Statements, Online Access, and Information Rights
Sections: Draft ACA (often silent or Customer-only)
Playbook: Duplicate statements to Agent; online view access; Customer authorization hard-coded.
Deviation: Silent or "upon request, subject to Bank policies."
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Agent blind to balances and leakage pre-enforcement; slower default detection.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 2.5. Accept Bank standard onboarding forms for view access if timeline is pre-funding or within short post-closing period.

ISSUE 13 — Notice of Adverse Claims, Legal Process, Freezes
Sections: Draft ACA Bank discretionary freeze rights
Playbook: Prompt notice to Agent of garnishment, levy, freeze, adverse claims, Account Agreement default, or Bank exit; no contractual freeze that impairs control except mandatory law/valid process.
Deviation: Bank may freeze for "compliance" or internal reasons without notice; no adverse-claim notice covenant.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Silent impairment of collateral; Agent learns too late to seek relief or inject funds protection.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 2.4(c). Acknowledge Bank must obey legal process; insist on parallel notice.

ISSUE 14 — Other Control Agreements / Priority of Competing Instructions
Sections: Draft ACA (typically silent)
Playbook: Bank represents it is not party to other control agreements on the accounts and will not enter any; Company covenant against other control arrangements except Loan Document–permitted junior arrangements with satisfactory intercreditor terms.
Deviation: Silent — Bank could already be bound to another secured party.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: UCC priority among conflicting control parties; potential stalemate or prime-out.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline §§ 3.1, 4.2. Obtain Bank rep as of signing; bring-down if delayed closing.

ISSUE 15 — Successor Administrative Agent / Assignment
Sections: Draft ACA (often requires all-party consent to assignment)
Playbook: Successor Agent under Credit Agreement steps in on written notice to Bank without Company consent; assignments consistent with Credit Agreement permitted.
Deviation: Amendments/assignments require Company and Bank consent in all cases.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Agency transfer friction; refinance or enforceability complications.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 5.3. Bank may condition on KYC of successor — acceptable if commercially reasonable and does not allow substantive consent right.

ISSUE 16 — Governing Law, Forum, Jury Waiver
Sections: Draft ACA miscellaneous
Playbook: New York law; exclusive Manhattan state/federal courts; mutual jury waiver; UCC mandatory choice-of-law savings for perfection.
Deviation: Bank home-state law and venue; no jury waiver; sometimes arbitration.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Inconsistent with Credit Agreement enforcement architecture; cost and predictability.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 6.3. Fallback: NY law with non-exclusive NY courts if Bank policy hard-blocks exclusivity — flag as Low residual if jury waiver and NY law obtained.

ISSUE 17 — Irrevocability; Coupled with Interest
Sections: Draft ACA (missing)
Playbook: Bank's control undertakings irrevocable and coupled with Secured Party's security interest; Customer cannot revoke Bank's duty to obey Agent while ACA is in force.
Deviation: Silent or Customer may amend account mandates freely.
Risk Rating: MEDIUM
Exposure: Customer revocation arguments; Bank hesitation mid-enforcement.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 6.7.

ISSUE 18 — Further Assurances
Sections: Draft ACA (missing or weak)
Playbook: Company and Bank further assurances reasonably requested by Agent to maintain control/perfection.
Deviation: Absent.
Risk Rating: LOW
Exposure: Friction on account renumbering, system migrations, joinders for new accounts.
Recommended Position: REQUIRE Redline § 4.3.

ISSUE 19 — Joinder / Future Accounts at Same Bank
Sections: Draft ACA schedule static
Playbook: Mechanism to add accounts by supplement/joinder without full renegotiation.
Deviation: No mechanism; new accounts left uncontrolled until full amendment.
Risk Rating: LOW / MEDIUM (elevates if Company frequently opens DDAs)
Exposure: Recurring perfection gaps; checklist thrash.
Recommended Position: Prefer simple supplement mechanic (Redline § 1.1 Deposit Accounts definition; § 2.4(b)).

ISSUE 20 — Fees and Expenses
Sections: Draft ACA fee provisions
Playbook: Company pays Bank's and Agent's reasonable documented costs of negotiation, administration, enforcement; consistent with Credit Agreement expense section.
Deviation: Bank fees open-ended or uncapped "professional fees"; attempts to charge Agent.
Risk Rating: LOW
Exposure: Economic leakage; limited legal risk.
Recommended Position: Company-pays model; reasonable/documented standard (Redline § 6.8).

ISSUE 21 — PATRIOT Act / Sanctions / KYC
Sections: Draft ACA (boilerplate variance)
Playbook: Standard PATRIOT notification; parties provide KYC info; no requirement to violate sanctions/law.
Deviation: Overbroad suspension rights without notice.
Risk Rating: LOW
Exposure: Operational holds; usually manageable with notice covenant (ties to Issue 13).
Recommended Position: Accept standard PATRIOT notice; add notice of any sanctions-related hold (Redline § 6.9 + § 2.4(c)).

ISSUE 22 — Third-Party Beneficiaries (Secured Parties)
Sections: Draft ACA (missing)
Playbook: Lenders/Secured Parties are express third-party beneficiaries of Agent's rights (or adequate Agency recognition).
Deviation: Strict privity; only named Agent.
Risk Rating: LOW
Exposure: Edge-case standing arguments if Agency vacancy occurs without succession mechanics.
Recommended Position: Include Redline § 6.6 together with successor-Agent clause.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. MISSING PROTECTIONS (GAP LIST)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The Draft ACA omits or inadequately treats the following Playbook-required protections (all inserted in aca-redline.docx):

  1. Express UCC control acknowledgment and "without further consent" formulation.
  2. Fixed NOEC implementation timing and multi-channel post-NOEC freeze.
  3. Form of Control Notice (Exhibit A).
  4. ACA-over-Account-Agreements supremacy clause.
  5. Narrow, closed set of Bank priority carve-outs; subordination of general banker's lien.
  6. Termination locked to Agent release/payoff/tri-party consent.
  7. Bank resignation conditioned on successor control agreement.
  8. Successor Agent recognition on notice.
  9. Obligations definition aligned to Credit Agreement.
  10. Duplicate statements / view access to Agent.
  11. Adverse claim and legal-process notice.
  12. Rep/covenant: no other control agreements.
  13. Irrevocability / coupled-with-interest clause.
  14. Further assurances; account-add joinder path.
  15. NY law, Manhattan forum, jury waiver.
  16. Secured Parties as third-party beneficiaries.
  17. Excluded Account alignment and Schedule I completeness representation.
  18. Controlled limitation of liability with NOEC-failure carve-out; no general Agent indemnity.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. OFF-MARKET TERMS AND RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION POSTURE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Off-market in favor of Bank/Customer (seek deletion or heavy modification):
  • Broad "all obligations" setoff seniority.
  • Unilateral 30-day termination.
  • Open-ended "reasonable time" to implement exclusive control.
  • Account Agreements control on conflict.
  • Agent indemnity of Bank.
  • Home-state exclusive venue with no jury waiver (when facility is NY-law).

Market-acceptable concessions (if needed to close):
  • Authentication procedures for NOEC that do not extend outside implementation date.
  • Modest numeric cap on ordinary fees/overdraft carve-outs.
  • "Final non-appealable judgment" qualifier on Bank negligence standard if NOEC-failure remains actionable.
  • Non-exclusive (vs exclusive) NY courts if exclusivity is a true Bank policy block — only with NY law + jury waiver retained.
  • Commercially reasonable KYC on successor Agent.
  • Bank professional-fee reimbursement by Company limited to reasonable documented out-of-pocket amounts.

Non-negotiable for Agent sign-off (Playbook "Red" items):
  • Valid § 9-104(a)(2) control language without Customer consent residual.
  • Effective NOEC mechanics with short fixed timing and post-notice freeze.
  • No unilateral termination; successor-Bank condition on resignation.
  • Subordination of general Bank setoff (narrow carve-outs only).
  • ACA supremacy over Account Agreements.
  • Obligations definition aligned to facility.
  • NY governing law (facility-aligned).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. EXPOSURE ANALYSIS (INTEGRATED)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Perfection / Priority Exposure: Issues 1–5, 8, 11, 14. In a Customer bankruptcy or competing-lien scenario, defective control or senior Bank setoff can convert expected cash collateral into unsecured or junior recovery. Magnitude scales with peak cash in the accounts (collections concentration risk).

Enforcement Timing Exposure: Issues 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 13. Even with paper perfection, slow or leaky exclusive control, silent freezes, or termination/resignation gaps create practical empty-bag risk at default.

Documentary / CP Exposure: Credit Agreement requires control agreements "in form and substance satisfactory to the Administrative Agent." Signing the Draft ACA as-is is not satisfactory; funding or post-closing checklist clearance should be withheld until Redline protections land or express written waivers are obtained from authorized Agent personnel.

Operational Exposure: Issues 11, 12, 19. Wrong accounts controlled (or right accounts omitted) create both compliance defaults and unintended control over excluded trust/payroll funds.

Intercreditor / Future Facility Exposure: Issues 14, 15, 22. Silence on competing control and awkward agency succession impairs amend-and-extend, uptier, or refinance optionality.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

| ID | Topic                              | Draft ACA § (Bank Form)     | Playbook / CA Requirement                  | Risk   | Disposition in aca-redline.docx      | Position        |

| 2  | NOEC timing                        | "Reasonable period"         | ≤1 BD confirm; next open implement         | HIGH   | § 2.3(b)–(c)                         | REQUIRE         |
| 3  | Post-NOEC channel freeze           | Partial / silent            | All Customer channels freeze               | HIGH   | § 2.3(d)                             | REQUIRE         |

| 6  | Unilateral termination             | 30-day notice               | Agent release / payoff / tri-party only    | HIGH   | § 5.1                                | REQUIRE         |
| 7  | Bank resignation                   | Silent / free exit          | Successor ACA condition                    | HIGH   | § 5.2                                | REQUIRE         |
| 8  | Secured Obligations definition     | Narrow / circular           | = CA "Obligations"                         | HIGH   | § 1.1                                | REQUIRE         |
